In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surah As-Saff (The Ranks)

It is Madani.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah﴾. We have already explained the meaning of this verse. In some reports: the most beloved speech to Allah, the Exalted, is "Subhan Allah" (Glory be to Allah), and because of His love for this phrase, He inspired it into the people of the heavens and the earth.

And His saying: ﴿And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾. We have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 61, verse 2:

The words of God Most High: ﴿O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: The Companions of the Messenger of God gathered and discussed the Resurrection and the matter of the Hereafter. Then they said: "If we knew what God loves, we would do it, and we would sacrifice our souls." 

In another narration: ʿAbdullah ibn Rawahah used to say to whoever he met: "Come, let us believe for an hour and remember God Most High." He would say: "I wish I knew what God loves so that I could do it." When God made jihad obligatory and commanded them to give up their souls and wealth, and prescribed fighting for them, they loved life and disliked fighting, so God Most High revealed His words: ﴿O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do?﴾

And from Qatadah: When the Companions of the Messenger of God fled on the day of Uhud, except for a small group of them, God Most High revealed this verse.

The verse, although general, applies to some of the Companions and not to others. God Most High said in another place: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God. Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow, and among them is he who awaits, and they have not changed in the least.﴾ This is clear evidence that the verse in this surah was not directed at all of them in a general sense.

In the exegesis (al-tafsir) it is related that ʿAbdullah ibn Rawahah said: "When the verse of jihad was revealed, I restrained my soul in the way of God." Then when he went out to the expedition of Mu'tah, "the Prophet had appointed Zayd ibn Harithah; if he is martyred, then Jaʿfar ibn Abi Talib; if he is martyred, then ʿAbdullah ibn Rawahah." [He said: Zayd was martyred.] Then Jaʿfar took the banner and was martyred; then ʿAbdullah ibn Rawahah took the banner and was martyred. Then Khalid ibn al-Walid took the banner and fought until he brought the Muslims back.

Qur'anic quotations are in ﴿ ﴾ markers. Translate the passage.

And His saying: ﴿Greatly hateful it is in the sight of Allah﴾, meaning: hatred (maqt, "severe hatred, detestation"), ﴿that you say what you do not do﴾. The meaning is: Allah the Exalted detests the one who says something and does not act upon it.

Tafsir al-Quran of al-Sam'ani, on surah 61, verse 4:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks, as if they were a structure joined firmly together.﴾ That is: fastened together, some of it to others. It was also said: they stand firm in battle against the disbelievers with the steadfastness of a building whose parts are placed upon one another and sealed with lead (rasas). When the Arabs build with stones, they fix the stones (yarussuna al-hijara) and then place them within the structure, and they call it the marsus building (al-bina' al-marsus).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 61, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when Moses said to his people, "O my people, why do you harm me, when you know that I am the Messenger of Allah to you?"﴾ We have already explained what it was that harmed Moses, peace be upon him, in Surah al-Ahzab.

And His saying: ﴿And when you know that I am the Messenger of Allah to you﴾ means: "and you know," and "qad" is a particle of emphasis (silah).

And His saying: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ means: they inclined away from the truth, [so] Allah caused their hearts to incline, that is, He increased them in inclination away from the truth.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾ means: the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 61, verse 6:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And when Jesus, son of Mary, said: "O Children of Israel, I am the Messenger of God to you, confirming what came before me in the Torah, and bringing good tidings of a Messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad."﴾ It is established by the narration of Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, that the Prophet said: "I have five names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am al-Mahi (the Eraser), by whom God erases disbelief; I am al-Hashir (the Gatherer), at whose feet people will be gathered; and I am al-Aqib (the Last), after whom there is no prophet." He, may God be pleased with him, said: Abu 'Ali al-Shafi'i informed us of this hadith, Ibn Faras informed us, Abu Ja'far al-Dibli informed us, Sa'id ibn (Jubayr) 'Abd al-Rahman al-Makhzumi informed us, from Sufyan, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father... the hadith.

And His words: ﴿But when he brought them the clear signs, they said, "This is plain magic."﴾ That is: manifest.

In the tafsir of al-Naqqash: the name of the Messenger in the Gospel is Faraqlit (Paraclete), and Jesus gave good tidings of him through the covenant that was taken from him. The covenant taken is in the words of the Exalted: ﴿And when God took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom, then there will come to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him."﴾ up to the end of the verse.

As for the meaning of his name Ahmad, there are two aspects. The first: because he used to praise God abundantly. The second: because people praised him for his deeds.

Qur'anic quotations are wrapped in ﴿ ﴾ markers per the instructions. The verse here is 61:7.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah while he is being invited to Islam? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ We have explained this previously.

Almighty Allah's words: ﴿They intend to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths﴾. It is said: it is the Qur'an. And it is said: it is Muhammad (ﷺ).

And His words: ﴿But Allah will perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it﴾, meaning: the matter of His light will be perfected, although the disbelievers dislike it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 61, verse 9:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it.﴾ That is: over all the religions, east and west. The full realization of the truth of this verse will occur only at the descent of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam (ʿĪsā, son of Maryam), when no religion remains except the religion of Islam.

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ Trade (tijarah) is that you give something and take something in return. So He made the expenditure of one's self and wealth, and the taking of reward, a trade, and this is in the manner of metaphor (majaz).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "Believe in Allah and His Messenger," and this is the meaning of the well-known recitation. Its answer (jawab) is: ﴿He will forgive you your sins﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿And strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if you only knew﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 61, verse 12:

His saying: ﴿He will forgive you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, meaning: gardens (basātīn). "The rivers" are the four rivers, which flow without a trench (ukhdūd).

And His saying: ﴿and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence (ʿAdn)﴾, meaning: they make them pleasant (yastaṭībūnahā). ʿAdn is the place of abiding. Ibn Masʿūd said: it is the middle (baṭnān) of Paradise. And in some reports: "Allah planted the Garden of ʿAdn with His own hand."

And His saying: ﴿That is the great triumph﴾, meaning: the great salvation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 61, verse 13:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And another [favour] you love﴾, meaning: you desire it.

And His saying: ﴿And another﴾, meaning: another quality. It was said: another trade.

And His saying: ﴿Help from Allah and an imminent victory﴾, it is the conquest of Makkah. It was said: it is the conquest of Persia and Byzantium.

And His saying: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾, meaning: of victory in this world, and of Paradise in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 61, verse 14:

His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, be helpers of Allah﴾. It is also recited: "anṣāran lillāh" (as helpers of Allah).

And His saying: ﴿as Jesus, the son of Mary, said to the disciples (al-Ḥawāriyyūn)﴾. The Ḥawāriyyūn are the elite and the choice ones of the prophets. From this is the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying to al-Zubayr: "He is the son of my paternal aunt and a ḥawārī from among my community." From this also comes ḥubz ḥawārī (ḥawārī bread), because of its whiteness and fineness. The Arabs call the women of the cities ḥawāriyyāt (the city women), and the poet said:

("So say to the city women, let them weep for others than us, and let only the barking dogs weep for us.")

In the narrative: Jesus, peace be upon him, gathered the disciples in a house, and they were twelve men, and he said: "Indeed one of you will disbelieve in me twelve times today," and so it was, as he said. He also said: "Who among you chooses to have my likeness cast upon him, and be killed and crucified?" A young man among them stood up and said: "I." He said: "Sit down." He repeated this three times, and each time that young man would stand up. Then Jesus said: "You are he." Then Allah the Exalted raised him from the rawzana (the niche/window) to the heaven, and the Jews entered, and Allah cast the likeness of Jesus upon that man, so they killed him and crucified him.

And His saying: ﴿Who are my helpers toward Allah?﴾, that is: with Allah. It was also said its meaning is: "Who are my helpers, who will be joined to Him in support" (min anṣārī ilā Allāh: "ilā" meaning "maʿa," with, joined to).

And His saying: ﴿The disciples said: We are the helpers of Allah﴾. Its meaning is apparent.

And His saying: ﴿So a faction of the Children of Israel believed, and a faction disbelieved﴾. In the exegesis: when Allah the Exalted raised Jesus, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, to the heaven, his companions differed. Some of them said: he was Allah, so he descended to the earth and then raised him to the heaven; these are the Nestorians. Some said: he was the son of Allah, whom He sent down to the earth, he did what He willed, then he ascended to the heaven; these are the Jacobites. Some said: he is the third of three, and the three are Father, Son and Spirit (zawj), and they said: three persons (aqānīm) who were pre-eternal, and Jesus is one of the three; these are the Melkites, and most Christians hold this. A people said: he is the servant of Allah and His messenger. So the faction of believers among the Children of Israel, before the Prophet, prevailed over the three factions. When the Prophet, peace be upon him, was sent, the believing faction prevailed over the three factions. This is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So We strengthened those who believed against their enemy﴾, that is: We gave them victory and made them strong.

And His saying: ﴿So they became dominant﴾, that is: victorious. And Allah knows best.
